answer: Cheap extra names fail when each identity must occupy one numbered sea-cliff ledge. An applicant posts 36 coins for 21 days on berth L-14 and hangs a one-use brass plate stamped with that berth serial. On the survey skiff's fourth dawn voyage a clerk photographs the plate beside the rail mark while the applicant logs comet 19P at the official 22° bearing. Peers attest only if the ledge registry lists one plate per berth, the bearing sits within 0.5° of the almanac, and the serial is unique. A borrowed plate or two names on one ledge burns the stake and seals the berth for 15 months.
